name: Alexandroupoli
title: Alexandroupoli Ship Gauging | UTM for LNG, Bulk & Ferries
description: Ultrasonic thickness gauging at Alexandroupoli, Thrace: LNG carriers, tankers, bulk and cargo ships, deck, hold and ballast tank thickness measurement.
h1: Alexandroupoli, Thrace: Hull Thickness Measurement for Energy and Cargo Ships
intro: Alexandroupoli, in Greek Thrace near the Turkish border, has become an energy gateway: an LNG floating terminal lies offshore, and gas carriers, tankers, bulk ships and ferries use the port. Many of these ships stay briefly, so the plan has to be exact. We send a team from India to the vessel, and the readings are scoped to the call.

highlights.p: Gas carriers calling at the floating terminal off Thrace come under strict operator and terminal rules. Any gauging of accessible structure is planned with the ship's manager and agent, well before arrival.
The port serves Thrace and the wider region, with bulk cargo, general cargo and military logistics traffic. Hold, hatch cover and deck readings follow cargo operations.
Alexandroupoli lies a short voyage from the Dardanelles and Marmara, and ships here are often between Black Sea and Aegean calls, with brief stops and tight schedules.

port.h: Alexandroupoli: an Aegean gateway in Thrace
p: Alexandroupoli lies on the north coast of the Aegean in the region of Thrace, not far from the mouth of the Evros river and the Turkish border. The port is managed by the Alexandroupoli Port Authority and consists of a main harbour with commercial quays and a ferry terminal, serving the city and the surrounding region. Ferries run to the island of Samothrace, and the port has long handled cargo for Thrace and the eastern Macedonia hinterland, with road and rail links north into Bulgaria and east toward Turkey.

In recent years the area has gained importance as an energy and logistics node. An LNG floating storage and regasification unit lies offshore south-west of the port, receiving cargoes from gas carriers and feeding the Greek gas network and onward to the Balkans, while the port itself has seen increased cargo and military logistics traffic. The result is an unusual combination of ship types for a regional port: gas carriers calling at the offshore unit, product tankers, bulk carriers and general cargo ships at the commercial quays, and ferries on the island service, together with vessels linked to the terminal's support operations.

Weather matters in the northern Aegean. Winter northerlies can be sharp, and summer winds affect the open coast. Ships at anchor off the port are generally in reasonable shelter, but launch transfers are decided by the master, and any work at the offshore terminal depends on operator rules and sea state. Because Alexandroupoli has no large repair yard, ships needing steel work move on to yards in other parts of Greece or in Turkey, and gauging here fits best as an early step, either during a cargo stop or at anchor between operations.

facilities.h: Where gauging can happen around Alexandroupoli
p: At the commercial quays, gauging is done alongside, subject to the port authority's ISPS arrangements and the agent. Bulk and general cargo ships offer open holds, hatch covers and coamings during discharge, while product tankers allow deck, deck piping and ballast tank readings within the terminal's rules. A ferry alongside for the day permits deck, ramp and accessible plating readings, and tank work is best done in lay-up.

Gas carriers are a special case. A carrier at an offshore LNG terminal is under tight operator rules and gauging there depends on operator permission, safe boarding and a defined window, so any work is arranged by the ship's manager well in advance and may not be possible during cargo operations. Ships at anchor off the port can be boarded by launch for pre-docking or condition work. There is no large drydock in the area, so heavy steel renewal is carried out elsewhere, and readings taken here help the owner plan that work.
list: Commercial cargo quays — hold, hatch cover, coaming and deck gauging on bulk and general cargo ships during discharge
Fuel and tanker berths — deck, deck piping and ballast tank readings on product tankers within terminal rules
Ferry terminal — deck, ramp and ballast tank readings on island ferries, best during lay-up
Anchorage off the port — pre-docking, pre-purchase and condition gauging, reached by launch
Offshore LNG terminal — accessible structure on gas carriers only where operator rules and ship safety permit

context.h: Port state control, energy rules and regional trade
p: Port state control at Alexandroupoli is carried out by the Hellenic Coast Guard under the Paris MoU. The Mediterranean emission control area for sulphur, in force since 1 May 2025, covers the Aegean. EU ETS has applied to shipping since 2024 and FuelEU Maritime since 2025. Ships calling at EU ports should also carry an Inventory of Hazardous Materials. For LNG carriers, owners and charterers apply their own vetting and class requirements, and the terminal operator may set additional conditions for anyone boarding.

The regional mix also affects timing. The ports of Thrace serve landlocked and near-border markets, and ships often call at Alexandroupoli between Black Sea, Turkish and Greek ports, with short berth stays. Owners of those ships may have no superintendent attending, so the report needs to be clear enough to act on remotely: readings tied to frame numbers, photographs of the worst areas and a summary of what needs attention before the next survey or charter inspection.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs at Alexandroupoli
jobs.p: Most jobs here are short and scoped around a berth stay or an anchorage wait. The superintendent defines the spaces and the window, the crew prepares them, and we report readings by area so decisions can be made before the ship sails. Energy-sector calls are planned in more detail, with terminal rules checked early.
list: Hold and hatch cover gauging on a bulk carrier discharging at the commercial quay, measured hold by hold as each is cleared.
Deck plating and deck piping readings on a product tanker at a tanker berth, ahead of an oil-major vetting inspection.
Pre-docking gauging of ballast tanks on an older general cargo ship at anchor, giving the manager a steel estimate for a yard elsewhere.
Deck, ramp and ballast tank gauging on a Samothrace ferry during winter lay-up to support the refit specification.
Accessible deck and ballast structure readings on an LNG carrier, where the operator, the manager and the terminal agree access in advance.

logistics: The team flies into Alexandroupoli's Dimokritos Airport, normally connecting through Athens, or into Thessaloniki and continues by road. Port passes, launch boarding and any terminal permits are organised by the ship's agent from crew lists and equipment details we send ahead. A Schengen visa issued in India is needed for every technician, since Greece follows the Schengen rules. Cargo and tanker calls here may be fixed at short notice, so telling us early about expected Alexandroupoli stops helps us keep a visa ready when the berth date is confirmed.

faqs.q: Can an LNG carrier be gauged at Alexandroupoli?
faqs.a: Only where the operator, the ship's manager and the terminal agree and safety allows. Access to accessible structure such as deck and ballast spaces has to be planned well in advance, and may not be possible during cargo operations. We review the terminal's boarding rules at enquiry and tell you early what looks realistic.

faqs.q: Is there a drydock near Alexandroupoli for steel renewal?
faqs.a: No large repair yard is available locally. Ships needing steel renewal move to yards in other parts of Greece or in Turkey. Readings taken here give the owner a measured basis for a steel estimate, help compare yard offers and allow plate to be ordered before the ship sails.

faqs.q: Can ships at anchor off Alexandroupoli be gauged?
faqs.a: Yes, subject to weather and the master's decision. The agent books a launch and we board with portable equipment. Tanks must be ventilated, tested and certified safe beforehand. Northerly winds can interrupt transfers, so we leave slack and inform the superintendent promptly if conditions narrow the window.

faqs.q: What can be done on a tanker alongside?
faqs.a: Mostly the weather deck, its piping and the ballast tanks, inside the berth operator's permit system. Cargo transfer may pause the work. The agent and terminal confirm what is allowed, and we plan readings so they fit around operations instead of delaying them.

faqs.q: Can one trip cover Alexandroupoli and Kavala?
faqs.a: Often. Both are in northern Greece and can be linked by road, so one mobilisation can cover several ships when dates align. Send us the vessels and windows, and we will arrange the order of jobs, the visa period and the agent contacts together.
